questions.question: Training memory overflows though the weights alone should fit. What else lives on the GPU?
options: Nothing; weights are the only memory
The training data целиком
Only the loss scalar
Master weights plus optimizer moments, multiples of the model
questions.explanation: Optimizer state dwarfs weights. This lesson shards it across ranks while keeping the model whole.

questions.question: For total=17, world_size=4, and rank=3, what does shard_bounds return?
questions.explanation: The padded chunk size is ceil(17/4)=5. Rank 3 starts at 15 and has a logical end min(20,17)=17, so the tuple is (15,17,5).

questions.question: Which sequence describes ZeroOptimizer.step after gradients are available?
options: Reduce-scatter summed gradients, divide by world_size, update the local Adam shard, then all-gather parameters
All-gather parameters, update every full Adam state, then discard gradients
Update only rank 0 and broadcast its loss
Reduce-scatter parameters and never reconstruct the full model
questions.explanation: The step flattens gradients, reduce-scatters their sums and averages, applies bias-corrected Adam to each local shard, then all-gathers master shards back into full parameters.

questions.question: What is the role of padding in a non-divisible flattened parameter vector?
options: It changes the model's parameter count permanently
It makes equal communication chunks; the padded tail is removed when real parameters are scattered back
It drops the last real parameters to preserve equal chunks
It allows ranks to use different optimizer learning rates
questions.explanation: Padding is only a communication layout convenience. The extra slots are zeros and are sliced away when the original-length parameter vector is reconstructed.

questions.question: For one rank's optimizer state, which storage is represented by shard_bytes?
options: Only the model's fp16 activations
The full model parameter vector plus one gradient buffer
One fp32 master shard plus its Adam m and v shards
The complete master, m, and v vectors replicated on every rank
questions.explanation: The memory table counts three fp32 arrays for the local chunk: master parameters, first moment, and second moment. It does not claim that all optimizer state is local.

questions.question: How does gather_flat_grads represent a parameter whose grad is None?
options: It skips the parameter and shifts every later offset
It raises because every parameter must receive a gradient
It copies the previous parameter's gradient
It inserts a zero tensor with the same shape before flattening
questions.explanation: A missing gradient contributes zeros of the parameter's shape, preserving a stable flat layout for reduce-scatter and later parameter updates.
